nonblocking.item: 2 (refute-invariants) Under pystachy run, lli's libraries shadow the library an @extern names, and an embedded CPython's extension modules
nonblocking.detail: A user @extern no longer links its library or uses lli -dlopen. When the def statement runs, pys_c_bind does dlopen(lib, RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL), adding RTLD_DEEPBIND under the JIT, then dlsym in that handle, as ctypes.CDLL does. The stub calls through @ffi.fp.<fn>. A missing library or symbol raises OSError or AttributeError with dlerror's text, as ctypes does (tests c_nolib and c_nosym record the message). For embedding under the JIT, pye_init sets sys.setdlopenflags(RTLD_NOW|RTLD_DEEPBIND). Results: the shadow test prints 42 and collide prints MINE-9.9 in all three runs, and e20_rl/rl2 get readline, not libedit, in the JIT. New test c_lib.py uses tests/ffi/ffitest.c, which defines zlibVersion and ZSTD_versionNumber. Documented residuals: sys.getdlopenflags() shows DEEPBIND under the JIT; @extern("") depends on what the process has loaded; AOT is the reference tier for embedding.

nonblocking.item: 3 (refute-invariants) Segfaults: Object(5) built from a raw pointer, and _text(PyObject_Str(e)) with NULL
nonblocking.detail: Object() called from outside lib/pyobj.py is a compile-time error, as is reading an Object's fields (tests/ffi/errors/py_ctor.py and py_field.py). The twin's Object() raises TypeError and uses a private _wrap. _text takes a fallback for NULL and encode failures. When str(e) fails, _raise raises the exception str() raised instead (once; else '<exception str() failed>'), in the twin and in pyembed.c's pye_fail alike. e11 is rejected at file:line; e16 and bs1 print 'caught bad str' / 'caught RuntimeError' like the twin. Test: py_badstr.py with side_badstr.py.

nonblocking.item: 4 (refute-invariants) The twins do not specify the native surface: ffi.track, pyobj internals, @extern keywords and defaults, to_float, the import-time exception class
nonblocking.detail:
Four parts fixed, the fifth documented.
- ffi.track, untrack and collected may be imported or called only from GLUE modules (lib modules that use ffi), and the twin no longer has them (test c_track).
- @extern("python") is reserved (test c_python).
- A program may use only a GLUE module's __all__, through from-import or a module attribute, and no field of its classes (tests py_private, py_modattr, py_field). The twin has the same __all__.
- The twin binds @extern calls with inspect.signature, so keywords and defaults work as the native code already allowed (e1_kw and e7_default are the same; c_libm tests them).
- The twin's to_float follows PyFloat_AsDouble (no str parsing) and to_int range-checks like PyLong_AsLongLong (test py_convert).
- Documented, not reproduced: an exception raised by an extension module's code at import leaves as its nearest builtin class, while the source run raises its own class. m1 is observed exactly as documented.

nonblocking.item: 5 (refute-invariants) Separate stdout/stdin buffers: only call() flushes, stdin read-ahead, the extension module's input() ignores sys.stdin
nonblocking.detail:
pyembed.c now owns the stdio hooks shared by embedding and ext (runtime.c's std_hook and in_hook).
- Embedded: pye_enter writes Pystachy's pending output before every operation; Python's sys.stdout or sys.stderr is flushed before Pystachy's next write to that stream; call() flushes Python's sys.stdout first, as the twin's call() does.
- A replaced sys.stdout (redirect_stdout, or None) receives Pystachy's prints.
- input(), sys.stdin.readline() and read() go through Python's input() and sys.stdin in both modes.
Results: e4_importprint, e10_stdin and ext c2 are the same. Tests: py_order, py_stdin (.in), py_redirect, ext rdclient.

nonblocking.item: 6 (refute-invariants) Automatic release does not bound Python memory: Python's memory never starts a collection
nonblocking.detail: pys_track(o, v, n) counts TRK_BYTES plus n, where n is sys.getsizeof (pye_sizeof) for results of attr, call, [] and import_module, and the str length for of_str. When the count reaches the limit, pys_track collects, as an allocation would. Before this, the count was checked only on the allocator's slow path, so e21 had 0 collections. e21's peak RSS is now 67 MiB against the twin's 27, where it was 2871. Test: py_big.py, run without GC stress, asserts a peak under 200 MiB.

nonblocking.item: 7 (refute-interop) The depth guard releases nothing during an outer call, and the 512-byte charge ignores object size
nonblocking.detail: Every pyobj operation now takes its own reference (_own, Py_IncRef) to each object it passes to CPython and releases it in its finally. _enter therefore drains the queue at any depth, and pyx_call also drains when the outermost call returns. The size is charged as in item 6. Results: x1 (1000 x 1 MiB inside one outer call) peaks at 42 MiB against the source's 13, where it was 1013; e1/big.py at 44 MiB against 11, where it was 1516. Test: ext/evl.py with memclient.py, run without stress.

nonblocking.item: 8 (refute-interop) An extension module never releases its Python references at interpreter exit
nonblocking.detail: exec_mod registers an atexit handler (pyx_exit). It releases every tracked reference (pys_trk_pop) and closes the module's open Pystachy files in order (pys_files_exit). Calls after that raise RuntimeError, so no Pystachy code can touch a released reference. Results: wr's a.txt and lg's log.txt contents after exit match the source run. Test: ext/wr.py with wrclient.py, through subprocesses. The 'right after the call' difference is the documented release-timing deviation; docs/ffi.md now says a file written through a dropped Object is flushed when it is released, and to close() it.

nonblocking.item: 9 (refute-interop) Embedded CPython uses the compat config: no C-locale coercion or UTF-8 mode, and sys.executable comes from PATH
nonblocking.detail: pye_preinit runs before Py_InitializeEx. In the C or POSIX locale with LC_ALL unset it applies PEP 538 coercion (setenv LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8 unless PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0), and it sets Py_UTF8Mode=1 (found with dlsym, since 3.15 does not need it) as PYTHONUTF8 or the C locale says. It also calls Py_SetProgramName with <prefix>/bin/python3 (or python3.X[t]), derived from dladdr of the loaded libpython. Results: loc.py on 3.13 (no locale) and 3.12 (LC_ALL=C), exe.py on 3.12 and 3.13, and mp.py on 3.14 are all the same in both tiers. Tests: py_utf8 (with PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0), py_coerce and py_exe.

nonblocking.item: 10 (refute-interop) Python's setlocale breaks Pystachy's float printing and parsing
nonblocking.detail: runtime.c now converts floats through fsnprintf and fstrtod, which switch to a C locale_t with uselocale only once c_num is set. c_num is set by pys_c_numeric, which runs from pye_init (embedding), pys_init_lib (ext) and pys_c_bind (any @extern). Programs without the FFI pay one null test, and their IR is unchanged. Results: fm2client, fmclient and fe2 under de_DE.UTF-8 are the same. Tests: py_locale.py and ext/fmclient.py; run.sh builds de_DE.UTF-8 into LOCPATH with localedef.

nonblocking.item: 11 (refute-interop) One process, two stdio buffers: output order only around call(), stdin never shared
nonblocking.detail: Same mechanism as item 5. In ext mode, out_hook is now pyembed.c's std_hook: a None sys.stdout makes print() a no-op, flush=True flushes the host's sys.stdout, and input() and sys.stdin read the host's sys.stdin, including a StringIO. Results: order.py, stdin2.py, rdclient.py and none.py are the same.

nonblocking.item: 12 (refute-interop) Unchecked NULLs: a str() that raises crashes the process, and argv decoding fails on non-UTF-8 bytes
nonblocking.detail: _text, _raise and pye_fail check every result. argv and sys.path[0] are decoded with surrogateescape, the init block checks errors after each step, and the GIL is released in a finally. Results: bs1 is the same in JIT and AOT; bx in ext mode prints 'caught RuntimeError' and the host no longer crashes; av.py with 'caf\xe9' gives the twin's argv. Tests: py_badstr, py_argv (.args) and ext/bx.py.

nonblocking.item: 13 (refute-recommendation) JIT symbol resolution happens in lli's process-wide scope
nonblocking.detail: Same mechanism as item 2, with the same results: collide.py prints MINE-9.9 and rl2.py gets readline history in the JIT. The jit_aot wording is corrected: C calls bind to the same library in both tiers. For embedding, JIT and AOT agree because of RTLD_DEEPBIND, AOT is named as the reference tier, and the residual differences are documented.

nonblocking.detail:
Py_SetProgramName with the libpython's own interpreter (item 9). Results:

design_changes: Rebased onto main's newest commit, 4dc548a (PRs #53, #101 and #102 merged Sunday 2026-10-11). base and irsame now refer to 4dc548a. The only conflict was tests/verify.sh, resolved by keeping both steps.

S1, @ffi.extern binds the way ctypes does. Nothing is linked any more: no lli -dlopen and no -l:lib. When the def statement runs, pys_c_bind opens the library (dlopen RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL, plus RTLD_DEEPBIND under the JIT), looks the symbol up with dlsym, and the stub calls through a stored pointer. A missing library or symbol becomes OSError or AttributeError with dlerror's text at the def, as in the twin. Calls take keywords and defaults. @extern("python") and ffi.track, untrack and collected are reserved for lib/pyobj.py. The answer is unchanged: both tiers, from the same IR, and JIT and AOT now bind the same library.

S2, pyobj's public API is exactly its twin's __all__ (Object, import_module, of_int, of_float, of_str, of_list). The compiler enforces this for GLUE modules (lib modules that use ffi): no other names, no Object() constructor, no fields. to_int and to_float follow PyLong_AsLongLong and PyFloat_AsDouble in the twin too.

S2 and S3, one stdout and one stdin across both runtimes. The draft planned to flush only around call(). Now pyembed.c's hooks write Pystachy's pending output before every operation, flush Python's stream before Pystachy's next write, route Pystachy's prints through a replaced sys.stdout, and read Pystachy's input() and sys.stdin through Python's (the host's in an extension module). pyembed.c is now linked into every extension module, compiled with -fexceptions.

Release is now owned and bounded. The depth guard is gone: each operation takes its own reference, so drops are released at any depth and on an extension module's outermost return. Each reference counts 512 bytes plus sys.getsizeof, and pys_track starts a collection when the count reaches the limit. The draft's flat 512 bytes checked only on the allocator's slow path did not bound memory. An extension module releases everything and closes its files in an atexit handler, then refuses calls.

Embedded CPython starts as python3 starts (pye_preinit): PEP 538 coercion and PEP 540 UTF-8 mode, which the compat configuration of Py_InitializeEx omits, and a program name taken from the loaded libpython, so sys.executable, sys.prefix and multiprocessing work, also without PYTHONHOME for relocatable builds. Under the JIT, the embedded CPython loads extension modules with RTLD_DEEPBIND. A failed flush at finalization exits 120.

The runtime's float text no longer depends on the locale once CPython or a C library shares the process (uselocale around snprintf and strtod). Plain programs pay one null test per conversion, and their IR is unchanged.
The recommendation names AOT as the reference tier for embedding. The JIT is supported, with documented residuals: sys.getdlopenflags() shows DEEPBIND, and lli's process differs for @extern("").

The test suite grew from 47 to 93 cases, with one regression test or more for each refuter issue. run.sh supports NAME.in, NAME.args and NAME.env, builds a test library and a de_DE locale, compares the error line of failing C-call tests, and runs py_big and memclient without GC stress.

remaining_issues: Ctrl-C in an embedding program does not finalize the embedded CPython: atexit handlers do not run, threads are not joined, and Python's buffered output is lost. This now also covers a Ctrl-C during input(), since reads go through Python. Only a Ctrl-C during the program's own write finalizes. Documented, not fixed: the SIGINT handler cannot run Python.

Release timing is still after a collection. A Python file written through a dropped Object gets its data only when the Object is released, at the latest at exit; close() is required to see it sooner (documented). sys.getsizeof is shallow, so a dropped container is charged its own size and not its items'. Peak memory stays one collector budget above CPython's.

Cost of correct output order: a Pystachy print after a pyobj operation costs about 440 ns more, because Python's sys.stdout is flushed first. attr, call and [] results cost about 60 ns more for sys.getsizeof.

Bytes reach the file descriptor at different times than in CPython's single buffer. Writes that bypass sys.stdout (os.write, child processes, C stdio) may interleave differently. This is documented; the text order is what is defined.

Under pystachy run, the embedded CPython loads extension modules with RTLD_DEEPBIND. This shows in sys.getdlopenflags(), and a module that relies on global-scope interposition behaves differently. AOT is the reference tier for embedding. @extern("") still depends on what the process has loaded (python3 links libz, lli has LLVM's dependencies, an AOT build only libc and libm). Both are documented.

The CPython-hosted compiler (python3 -m pystachy run) passes its own PEP 538 LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8 on to the program, so an embedded CPython starts in a UTF-8 locale with UTF-8 mode off before 3.15. Documented; tests/ffi skips py_coerce under the hosted compiler.

Extension modules: an exception raised at import leaves as its nearest builtin class (documented). sys.stdout.write with sys.stdout = None does nothing, where CPython raises AttributeError. Calls after the host's atexit handlers raise RuntimeError. Free-threaded 3.13t and 3.14t cannot load the modules. abi3 on 3.11 fails with the loader's generic ImportError. Stack switching (greenlet) is unsupported and undetected.
Stdin that C stdio read ahead before pyobj is first imported cannot be read by Python (documented).
tools/abi_check.sh is not yet in make verify or CI: it needs Misc/stable_abi.toml, which the repo does not vendor.

tests/ffi/c_nosym.out records the Debian/Ubuntu libm path (/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6) in dlerror's message. On CI runners without a shared libpython, the ffi verify step still skips the embedding and extension cases.

Unchanged from stage 3: tests/ffi/ext/mg.py builds with ext but is rejected by run and ir, because its main block calls an export. PYTHONHOME can leak into the hosted compiler when run.sh gets a relocatable PY.

Environment: ruff 0.16.8 is installed, not the pinned 0.17.0. Only x86-64 Linux with glibc was tested. pyembed.c's program-name derivation assumes a <prefix>/lib or <prefix>/lib/<multiarch> layout and leaves CPython's default otherwise.
